3390: A star of Utsunomiya, a track that closed in 2005, and winner of the Tochigi Triple Crown. He won 2 quickly at 3 (old age system), then kept missing until spring at 4, when he won the Shimotsuke Satsuki Sho, the Tochigi Derby easily, and the Shimotsuke Kikuka Sho for the Triple Crown. He hit his peak with 7 straight wins late at 6 into 7, but at 8 he was killed in a traffic accident on the way back from training.
2675: Debuting late, in December at 2, he won his debut and a 5-million race, then was 2nd to Blast Onepiece in the Mainichi Hai and to K A Knotech in the NHK Mile C., and rested instead of the Derby. 13th in the St. Lite Kinen, he won the Chunichi Shimbun Hai as favorite after a fierce duel. Older he mostly disappointed, top five only in the Lord Derby CT and Naruo Kinen. Then at 6, last choice of 10 in the March Kinko Sho, he led all the way and held off hot favorite Daring Tact by a neck - his first win in 2 years 4 months. At 7, 5th in the Kinko Sho and 4th in the Naruo Kinen, he retired after the Chunichi Shimbun Hai.
1885: Like other long-lasting Mayano Top Gun runners such as Precise Machine, Meisho Tokon and Chakra, he reached open class with the Namba S. (OP) at 5, then went nearly 3 years without a win. In the Osaka-Hamburg C. (OP) in spring at 8, last choice of 18 at 477 to 1, he charged to a neck 2nd behind Beat Black. Then as 7th choice he won the Meguro Kinen and the Hakodate Kinen, stunning everyone. He raced until 9 without regaining that shine.
1065: Winner of the 1975 Satsuki Sho and Derby and Horse of the Year. His 9 straight wins, from his debut at 3 (old age system) to an open race in spring at 5, are the JRA flat record. But more than records, Kaburaya O is remembered for his wild front-running, called "killer laps" and "insane pace." After winning the Tokyo Yonsai S. (now Kyodo News Hai) and Yayoi Sho, he led the Satsuki Sho at a blistering 58.9 for the first 1000m and pulled away in the straight for a record win. Lake Sprinter, who dueled him, broke a leg in the race and was put down, giving rise to the feared names. After the NHK Hai, he led the Derby even faster, 58.6 for 1000m. Surely he couldn't last 2400m - yet, mouth open and wandering in the straight, he held everyone off and won, amazing fans. No horse has since won the Derby leading at such a pace. Injury ruled out the Kikuka Sho; back in spring at 5 he won 2 dirt races and 1 on turf, but another injury forced his retirement. At stud he sired Queen Elizabeth Cup winner Miyama Poppy and Derby runner-up Grandpa's Dream. His camp later revealed his front-running was a tactic born of his timid nature and rare heart-lung capacity.
2451: A dirt sprinter who won open races like the Green Channel C. and Polaris S., then Saga's Summer Champion at 6 as hot favorite at 1.8, leading all the way. After a dry spell he won Korea's invitational Korea Sprint, then the Hyogo Gold T. At 8 he led all the way in the Tokyo Sprint, was 2nd in the Sakitama Hai and Tokyo Hai, then won the JBC Sprint as 4th choice - Christophe Lemaire, on a run of 3 straight weekly G1 wins, delivered again with a perfect ride from up front.
3180: A speedster who won the 2023 CBC Sho and Kitakyushu Kinen, champion of the Summer Sprint Series. Tried early in graded races (12th Keio Hai 2yo S., 18th Arlington C., 14th Aoi S.), she rested long, restarted at 4 and quickly reached the 3-win class. 16th in the Hakodate Sprint S., she won the CBC Sho, then led all the way in the Kitakyushu Kinen to top the series. 4th in the Sprinters S. (G1); unplaced in the BC Turf Sprint and Hong Kong Sprint.
